rv.q: With these two actors, it makes you feel complicit as you watch and laugh at this ersatz Lincoln and Booth performing their sad-sack realities for your pleasure and enjoyment.
Topdog/Underdog feels classic Steppenwolf but also contemporary and gripping.
This needs to be said: the chemistry between two great actors is palpable and consistent.
This is a stellar rendition of this complicated tale.

At one time, Lincoln was a hustler who had great skill at the game called "three-card monte", a street con game that at one time was played to con tourists in major cities. He no longer does this, but Booth, has been trying to master the game so that he can be "the man".
Leon's production made me see Topdog/Underdog differently, turning our act of watching into part of the play's unsettling equation.

cn.t: Critics hail this "blistering" and "heartbreaking" production of Parks' Pulitzer winner as a captivating American tragedy, with stellar performances by Davis and Smallwood bringing urgency to its timeless exploration of brotherhood and generational trauma.
